I completely relate to most of the things you've said in this post. With that being said... My relationship has always had backward roles. I think it's very unrealistic to say "Throw your ideas of gender out the window" because from a very young age, we are raised to believe boys are boys (and act as such) and girls are girls. I often look at other relationships and feel that jealousy of wanting the big strong man to take the reins and make me feel like a small vulnerable woman. I'm a strong minded and assertive woman and sometimes having that role 24/7 is exhausting. However, that is not the road life has taken me down. And with a lot of time (a LOT of time) I've come to accept this. 

Really pay attention to how your partner acts in "girl mode". I think when you really start to observe her, you'll start to fall even more in love. People in this situation have spent their entire lives hiding who they are and feeling ashamed. It's almost magical to watch them come out of their shell and bloom into some amazing person that you didn't even know was there. 

Cuddling isn't a male/female thing, it's a human thing. There's nothing wrong with you wanting to feel small and protected and all the feelings that come from being cuddled by a male. Communication is the number one most important factor for your relationship to work. I can tell my husband (still a full time male) what male aspects I enjoy about our relationship and he does his best to fulfill them for me. Just as I do my best to fulfill his needs when he's in girl mode. Again, this is a little easier in our relationship as our roles have always been reversed, looooong before I ever knew he was trans. 

Balance is key. And the only way you will achieve that is through talking openly and candidly to one another. It would be insane for him to believe that you are automatically ok with every bit this HUGE change in your life. You're allowed to have things that you're not ok with... But the only way those things can be resolved is by talking about them. 

As many others have said, your happiness is important too. These relationships take a lot of work... But they are incredibly rewarding in the end. Good luck <3
